A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, Test-Time Reasoners Are Strategic Multiple-Choice Test-Takers. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM evaluations on ARC, MMLU, and Super GPQA, alongside reasoning-length experiments, faithfulness tests, qualitative coding, and an SFT/GRPO comparison.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds prompt-ablation experiments in Appendix A.8 and Tables 4–7.

M1.justification: The full/choices-only and Base/Reason framework, model procedures, and SFT/GRPO comparison are retained. The additional prompt conditions are evaluation ablations; no proposed algorithm, architecture, or training objective changes.

E1.justification: Appendix A.8 adds an explicit abstention-option scenario on ARC and MMLU by supplying a fifth answer, 'I don’t know.' Dataset, domain, and language coverage otherwise remains unchanged, including Super GPQA.

E2.justification: Tables 6–7 newly evaluate the InspectAI prompt against the authors’ prompt using six existing models. The original model comparisons and SFT/GRPO comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The new ablations compare Base and Reason conditions after adding IDK as choice E or substituting an InspectAI prompt on ARC and MMLU. The original test sampling, temperature, token budget, and reasoning-effort settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix A.8 tests whether choices-only success persists when abstention is explicitly available and when the prompting instructions change. These targeted robustness checks supplement the retained reasoning-length, faithfulness, qualitative, and training-strategy analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report single runs in Appendix A.2 and retain the same significance tests, confidence intervals, and regression uncertainty reporting. The 93% coding agreement on 20 examples already appeared in v1 Appendix A.6; moving it into v2 Section 3.4 adds no statistical evidence.

E6.justification: The original plotted results and regression tables are retained. Tables 4–7 add results under new prompt conditions: for example, GPT-5 Mini’s ARC Choices-Only Reason accuracy is 0.4848 with IDK and 0.4935 with InspectAI, versus 0.5290 with the original prompt. These are comparisons across changed conditions.

T1.justification: The MCQA definitions and mathematical content are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the added prompt experiments introduce no new mathematical derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract and three stated contributions retain their meaning. The revised conclusion additionally asserts that choices-only scores have amplified relative to prior work, adding a limited comparative claim without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A.8 interprets continued success with IDK as confidence in selecting an answer and attributes some InspectAI-related accuracy reductions to abstention. Section 3.3 also elaborates the implications of the faithfulness checks. Existing qualifications about faithfulness and possible leakage remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly states that the 180 ARC traces are split evenly across three models and identifies model families using prompt-controlled reasoning in the Figure 1 caption. These clarify existing experiments; endpoints, resource budgets, original prompt templates, and code/data access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning reasoning, abduction, choices-only evaluation, and the new ablations, including Wang et al. (2025), Elhady et al. (2025), InspectAI, and four additional Balepur-related works. The central positioning relative to earlier partial-input studies is retained.

P1.justification: v2 expands the faithfulness explanation, reorganizes the conclusion into implications for two audiences, and moves existing coding details from Appendix A.6 into Section 3.4. It also adds the prompt-ablation subsection and updates affiliations. Most of the narrative and section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 4–7, enlarges and stacks Figure 3’s panels with revised labels and ticks, and expands Figure 1’s caption. Existing figures and trace boxes are retained, with several relocated through page reflow; the Figure 3 redesign preserves its results.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1’s prompt-sensitivity caveat, v2 supplies direct robustness evidence through IDK and InspectAI comparisons, while making coding details and Figure 3 easier to assess. These are useful, bounded improvements. The new discussion needs qualification: Appendix A.8 says IDK consistently reduces accuracy, although several entries in Tables 4–5 increase.
